q: Does the paper's RBE_SLD = 3.7 (U2OS) survive a full Lea-Catcheside joint fit with the T -> infinity extrapolation, or is it partly an artifact of the specific mixed-Medras-anchored fit protocol?
basis: Our direct Eq. (8) reading of the released supplementary survival data gives RBE_SLD = 2.0-2.3, i.e. 25-40% lower than the paper's headline 2.8-3.7. Both numbers are extracted from the same underlying spreadsheet (MOESM2 Supp Data 3), so the difference must lie in the fit ansatz. The abstract's central claim RBE_SLD > 2.5 is only marginally supported by our reading. This is a genuine partial-disagreement, not sampling noise.
next_steps: Implement a full Lea-Catcheside two-parameter joint fit (mu, RBE_SLD together) across all four dose-pair conditions and all inter-fraction intervals simultaneously, using scipy.optimize.least_squares with fit uncertainties from the covariance matrix. Compare the fitted RBE_SLD from that pipeline against both our Eq. (8) direct reading and the paper's 2.8/3.7. Free-endpoint pipeline: uicgpu Python + scipy, no external calls.

q: Does a genuine TOPAS-nBio simulation on the paper's simple-nucleus geometry reproduce their Fig. 4 (128.5 DSB/Gy at 129 keV/um, RBE_DSB = 3.67), or does it also disagree with the analytical surrogate direction?
basis: Our analytical simple-nucleus surrogate gives 216 DSB/Gy at 129 keV/um (RBE_DSB ~ 6.2) --- a factor of 1.7 higher than the paper. We attribute this to omitted ionisation-cluster substructure, SSB-pair saturation, and radial dose in the surrogate, but we have not independently verified the paper's TOPAS-nBio value. If TOPAS also lands near 216 instead of 128.5, the analytical model would be vindicated and the paper's Fig. 4 anchor would be questioned.
next_steps: Run TOPAS-nBio v3.9 (Geant4-DNA scorer) on uicgpu: 2.5 um spherical water nucleus, alpha at 5.4 MeV (matching Am-241 in the paper), 1 Gy delivered dose, DSB pair criterion 3.2 nm intra-track opposite strands, ~10^4 histories. Compare DSB/Gy against the paper's 128.5 and our surrogate's 216. TOPAS-nBio is already installed on uicgpu (free); estimated 4-6 h wall on one A100.

q: Do the Medras (McMahon & Prise 2021) mechanistic simulations in the paper's Fig. 5a-b top panels agree with our analytic cluster-foci fits, or does the mechanistic model give qualitatively different repair kinetics?
basis: We reproduced the cluster-foci Poisson-mixture model (Fig. 5c-d) analytically and got N_cl = 10.5 (PC-3), 12.6 (U2OS) --- within 5% of the paper's 9.9 and 10.2. But this is a phenomenological fit, not the Medras mechanistic prediction. We have no independent test that Medras itself, when told to score 'observable foci as one-or-more-unrepaired-DSB clusters', produces the same kinetics.
next_steps: Clone the Medras GitHub repository (github.com/sjmcmahon/Medras or similar), configure with the paper's cited parameters (k_simple = 1.4/h, k_complex = 0.16/h, alpha complex fraction 0.85, X-ray complex fraction 0.43), run for 5-10 Gy of each radiation quality, extract simulated foci-time series, and compare against our cluster-foci fits and the paper's Fig. 5. Free: Medras is open-source Python. Estimated 1-2 d including reading the repo.

q: Is the mixed-field additive LQ model (Eq. 2) actually superior to a simpler multiplicative or maximum-of-two model when tested on the mixed-field data, or is the additive form assumed rather than earned?
basis: The paper uses Eq. 2 (Zaider-Rossi-style square-root cross term) as its default mixed-field model and shows visual agreement with the data (Fig. 2 dashed lines). Our reproduction confirms the visual agreement, but neither the paper nor our replication has formally compared the additive model to alternatives via information criteria (AIC/BIC/F-test). The 'match' verdict at C11 is thus visual only.
next_steps: For each mixed-field dose point in Supp Data 2, compute predicted SF under three models: (a) Eq. 2 additive, (b) multiplicative SF_x * SF_alpha, (c) min(SF_x, SF_alpha), and (d) a saturating model. Report AIC per model and a formal F-test on the additive vs multiplicative pair. Pure numpy/scipy on free compute (uicgpu). ~1 h.

q: How robust is Table S1's beta_alpha = 0 assumption? Does allowing beta_alpha to float within a plausible range (e.g. 0-0.1 Gy^-2) meaningfully change the LQ fits and downstream RBE_D10 and RBE_SLD values?
basis: The paper fixes beta_alpha = 0 without a prior sensitivity check, and our replication inherits that assumption (finding chi^2/dof ~ 1 with the fixed value, which is consistent but not a strong test --- fixed parameters cannot fail their own fit). But at only 3-4 dose points per cell line, the LQ fit is under-constrained enough that a small beta_alpha shift could pull alpha_alpha by 10-15%.
next_steps: Refit the alpha clonogenic data for both cell lines with beta_alpha as a free parameter, report the fitted value with its uncertainty and the corresponding shifted alpha_alpha, then recompute RBE_D10 and (via Eq. 8) RBE_SLD. If the fitted beta_alpha is consistent with zero within 1sigma, the paper's simplification is vindicated; if it's non-zero, the downstream RBE numbers need widening. Pure scipy.optimize.curve_fit on the released Supp Data 2. Free. ~30 min.
